data.description:
# Ship release must verify in-scope work items are actually closed before reporting success

**Headline:** The ship release close step trusts `wl close`'s exit code and reports "All N work item(s) closed successfully" even when some closes were lost by the concurrent-`wl sync` race. It must re-read persisted state, retry once, and report unclosed items by id instead of claiming blanket success.

## Problem statement

`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` closes each release candidate with `wl close <id> --force --reason "Shipped in v<version>"` and treats a zero exit code as success, never re-reading the item to confirm the persisted `status`/`stage`. A lost close (the `wl` lost-update race, WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ) is therefore reported as a successful release — the operator only discovers dangling `in_review` work items after the fact.

## Users

- **Release operator / producer** running `/skill:ship release` — needs an accurate post-release close count so released work items are truly terminal.
- **Ship agent** executing the release pipeline — needs a verifiable close step so its summary and return value reflect reality.

Example user stories:

- As a release operator, I want the ship skill to report the true number of work items actually closed, so that I do not discover dangling `in_review` items after the release.
- As a ship agent, I want a close that exits 0 but did not persist `completed`/`done` retried once and, if still unpersisted, reported explicitly by id, so that lost closes are never silently counted as successes.

## Existing state

- `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` (`run-release.js`) builds the `closable` set (after producer-review overrides, cascade, and out-of-scope refusals), then loops calling the injected `runCloseCommand(item.id, reason)`; a non-throwing call increments `closedCount`.
- On zero errors it prints and returns `All ${closedCount} work item(s) closed successfully.` — no re-read of persisted state.
- The read boundary already exists in the codebase: `getItemLifecycleFn` / `getItemLifecycle` (from `check-final-validation.js`) returns `{id, status, stage}` and is already injected for descendant terminal-state checks.
- Demonstrated failure: ToneForge v0.1.2 release (2026-10-06) reported 53/53 closed but only 50 became `completed`/`done`; three items remained `completed`/`in_review` with no close comment and unchanged `updatedAt` (TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18, TF-0MUUELBUD002OEQ8, TF-0MMZIW9NQ09MV98G).

## Desired change

After each `runCloseCommand()` call (and once more after a bounded retry), read the item's persisted lifecycle and only count it as closed when `status === "completed"` **and** `stage === "done"`. Concretely:

1. Inject a verification read boundary (reuse `getItemLifecycleFn`, or add a dedicated `getCloseStateFn`/`verifyClosedFn` defaulting to `getItemLifecycle`).
2. Count and report `unclosedCount` / `unclosedItems` (`[{id, title, reason?}]`); never include unclosed items in `closedCount` and never emit a blanket "all closed successfully" when any attempted close did not persist.
3. Retry each unverified close **once** (bounded), re-verify, then report unclosed if still not terminal.
4. Keep the step non-blocking (failures are reported, not fatal) and preserve existing override, cascade, refusal, and `--dry-run` behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` verifies persisted state via an injectable read boundary for each attempted close instead of trusting only the close command's exit code.
2. An item that exits 0 but is not `completed`/`done` is counted as unclosed and listed by id; the summary and return value reflect it and never claim blanket success.
3. A transient lost close is retried at least once before being reported unclosed.
4. Regression tests with injected `getCandidateItemsFn` / `runCloseCommand` / verification boundary cover: (a) all closes persist → success; (b) one close is a no-op (exit 0, state unchanged) → retried, then reported unclosed; (c) retry re-persists → reported closed.
5. `npm run build` and the existing ship suites pass (no `wl` mutation from unit tests).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably `skill/ship/SKILL.md`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test isolation (SA-0MSJ2XMQL006CVQS):** unit tests must inject fakes; the verification boundary must be injectable and never hit the live worklog from the suite.
- **Non-blocking step:** unclosed items must not fail the release exit code (consistent with the existing close step); the fix changes reporting/return-value accuracy, not release gating.
- **Bounded retry:** at least one retry, no unbounded loop.
- **Terminal definition:** `status === "completed"` and `stage === "done"`.
- **Fail-safe on unreadable state:** if the verification read throws or returns `null`, treat the item as unverified/unclosed (never count it closed).
- **Preserve existing behaviour:** producer-review overrides, descendant cascade, out-of-scope refusals, and `--dry-run` (no mutation) must be unaffected.
- Root-cause fix of the `wl` race is out of scope (tracked on the ContextHub side).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()`: add injectable post-close verification, bounded retry, and `unclosedCount` / `unclosedItems` in the summary and return value; update the JSDoc `@returns` contract.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — add regression tests for all-persist success, no-op-then-unclosed (retried), and retry-repersists cases using injected boundaries.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — document the verify-and-retry close behaviour and the new unclosed reporting (Step 12 close work items).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — existing `getItemLifecycle` read boundary reused for verification (no functional change expected).

## Related work

- **WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ** (ContextHub) — root-cause fix: lock `wl close` against the lost-update race; child of WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7. Out of scope here; this item adds detection/visibility.
- **SA-0MUX8PYAY0008HFZ** — the raw race report refiled to ContextHub.
- **SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP** — ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done` (fixed by SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9 / SA-0MUTYRYEM000EEF7).
- **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** — parent-coverage and out-of-scope rules for child audits.
- **SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP** — cascade children of an audit-approved parent to `completed`/`done`.
- **SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q** — release-ready parent must override/absorb `needsProducerReview` on children.
- **SA-0MSJ2XMQL006CVQS** — test isolation: unit suite must never mutate the live worklog.
- **SA-0MSAL2NQV0008HY5** — audit runner stuck `in_progress` broke the release close step.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** added verification issues one `wl show` per attempted close (plus one per retry) — bounded by the candidate count; acceptable overhead for a release-time step.
- **Risk:** if the race also swallows the retry, the item is still reported unclosed — this is the intended visibility, not a regression.
- **Risk (scope creep):** "fix it in `wl` so closes never get lost" must be resisted here; record it as linked work on the ContextHub item rather than expanding scope.
- **Assumption:** `getItemLifecycle` reflects the persisted state immediately after a successful `wl close` completes (no eventual-consistency delay beyond process exit).
- **Assumption:** `stage: done` is the terminal stage and `status: completed` the terminal status for a closed item.
- **Failure mode:** a `wl show` timeout/throw makes the item unverifiable → treated as unclosed (fail-safe), so the release never over-reports.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required. The seed context (the refiled ToneForge v0.1.2 race report plus the existing detailed work-item description) specified the failure, the required behaviour, and the acceptance criteria. Context was verified by repository inspection (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `run-release.js`, the injected `getItemLifecycleFn` boundary, and `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs`).

- Q: (not asked) Is `getItemLifecycle` an adequate verification boundary, or is a dedicated one needed? — Resolution: reuse `getItemLifecycleFn` where possible, or add a dedicated injectable `getCloseStateFn` defaulting to `getItemLifecycle`; either satisfies AC1. Source: repository inspection of `run-release.js` / `check-final-validation.js`.
